match.reason: The closest bank point, Cells as the building blocks of life, covers only the first two parts of cell theory and never says that new cells come only from existing cells, so it does not teach the full new point and adding that idea would be a change of content, not a small adaptation.

draft.title: Cell theory
card: All living things are made of one or more cells. A cell is the smallest unit that can carry out the functions of life.
New cells come only from cells that already exist. A cell divides to make new cells.
Some organisms are made of one cell, such as bacteria. Others are made of many cells, such as a gum tree or a person.
Cell theory is an idea built from the evidence of many scientists. It lets us say that a living thing, big or small, is made of cells.
draft.remember: Living things are made of cells, and cells come from other cells.

a.q: A student looks at a pond sample and sees a tiny organism made of a single cell. What does cell theory say about this organism?
opts: It is alive, because living things are made of cells
It is not alive, because it has only one cell
It is alive only if it has more than one cell
It is made of cells that formed from non-living matter
a.why: Cell theory says all living things are made of one or more cells, so one cell is enough. Saying a living thing needs many cells is tempting, but the card says some organisms are a single cell.
a.clue: How many cells can a living thing have?

b.q: Mia finds a new type of cell growing in a dish in her school lab. Which idea from cell theory tells her where these cells came from?
opts: They came from cells that already existed
They formed from the nutrients in the dish
They formed from the water in the dish
They appeared from non-living matter over time
b.why: Cell theory says new cells come only from cells that already exist, so the dish must have held cells to begin with. Nutrients and water are needed for growth, but they do not make new cells by themselves.
b.clue: Where do new cells come from, according to the card?

a.best: It is alive, because living things are made of cells

b.best: They came from cells that already existed

problems.detail: "A new type of cell" is confusing. It can suggest a kind of cell that never existed before, which sits awkwardly with the idea that cells come only from existing cells. "Some cells growing in a dish" would be clearer.

The right option reasons the wrong way round. It says the organism is alive because living things are made of cells, but cell theory says living things are made of cells, not that anything made of cells is alive. The stem already calls it an organism, so the reasoning could mislead. Something like "A single cell is enough to make up a living thing" would be more accurate.
